questions.question: Does forward-model inversion (physics MAP/MLE in log-conductivity with multistart, or hybrid learned-init + Levenberg-Marquardt) achieve lower validation rel_l2 than the strongest purely learned regressor on the 80-dim sensor features?
Among learned regressors (ridge baseline, kernel_ridge, torch_mlp, extra_trees), which gives the lowest validation rel_l2, and does log target transform or noise augmentation help?

Are all four conductivities locally identifiable from the four sensors over the finite window, or do per-target errors reveal poorly constrained segments (e.g., outer segments near Dirichlet boundaries where the Gaussian pulse carries little signal)?
